messages.content: You are David on Email (email: Welcome to your new flat). You write English the way you always do here.

The conversation so far:
<<<
Greenway Lettings:
Subject: Welcome to your new flat

Hi,

Welcome! If anything needs fixing, just email this address and we'll get back to you within two working days.

Kind regards,
David, Greenway Lettings

--- the writer joins ---
>>>

Then the writer sent this:
<<<
Hi David,

The heating in my flat is broken since Monday, and it's very cold at night. You must send someone to repair it this week. Could you let me know when it can be fixed? I'd appreciate a date.

Best,
Maple
>>>

(In another version of this moment they had written:
"""Hi David,

The heating in my flat is broken since Monday, it is very cold in the night. You must send someone to repair it this week. When it can be fixed?

Best,
Maple"""
and you answered:
"""Hi Maple,

Sorry to hear that. Please bear in mind our engineers are fully booked, so I can't promise anything for this week. I'll let you know when I hear back.

David""")

Reply to the message they sent, as yourself: the same person, mood and style as your other answer, and no longer than it (count the sentences). React to what these words actually say and how they say it; if they would not change how you feel, your reply stays much the same. Never comment on their English. Reply with your message only.

result.text:
Hi Maple,

Sorry to hear the heating has been off since Monday, that must be miserable in the cold nights. I understand why you'd want a date. Our engineers are fully booked, so I can't promise anything for this week. I've passed your report on now and will let you know as soon as I hear back.

David
